title: Seven students sign the Pledge
text: In an attic room of a stone building in downtown Schenectady — West College, at Union and College streets — seven Union College undergraduates sign a formal pledge to organise a secret society. The Pledge, long kept as a piece of tawny paper in the archives of the Theta, bears the date 24 November 1833.

title: The first Constitution is adopted
text: The Minute Book of the Theta records the adoption of the Fraternity's first Constitution. The signed document was lost for a century and rediscovered in 1936 in the shop of a dealer in old and rare manuscripts; it is now in the archives of the Executive Council.

title: The first initiate
text: John H. E. Beach, class of 1838, becomes the first man initiated after the adoption of the Constitution.

title: The Diamond Badge is first worn in public
text: The badge was designed by Luke F. Newland, a noted Albany jeweller, who had been consulted by a committee including the founder Dr. Charles Washington Harvey.

title: The mother chapter takes the name Theta
text: The original chapter adopts the name Theta, at the instance of Maunsell Van Rensselaer, class of 1838, later President of Hobart College. The same year Merwin Henry Stewart becomes the first of the seven founders to die.

title: The first Convention
text: Psi Upsilon holds the first convention of any American fraternity.

title: The first membership catalogue
text: Psi Upsilon issues the first fraternity membership catalogue.

title: The first songbook
text: The Fraternity prints the first of its songbooks. Every printed songbook since has carried two epigraphs — one from The Merchant of Venice, and one by Francis M. Finch, Beta 1849, who wrote many of the earliest Psi U songs.

title: The first fraternity magazine
text: Psi Upsilon founds the first fraternity magazine.

title: The Convention Records begin
text: The earliest Convention Records held in this museum are those of the thirty-ninth annual Convention, held with the Gamma at Amherst College.

title: The Diamond begins
text: The first number of The Diamond of Psi Upsilon appears. It runs until 1887, is revived in 1920, and continues in print until 2015.

title: Garnet and gold
text: The Fraternity colours are chosen at the Convention of 1878.

title: A brother becomes President of the United States
text: Chester A. Arthur, Theta 1848, elected Vice President in 1880, becomes President on the assassination of James Garfield. He serves until 1885.

title: The system of heraldry is adopted
text: A committee of Albert P. Jacobs, Phi 1873; Karl P. Harrington, Xi 1882; and George B. Penny, Chi 1885, reported in 1892 on a system of arms for the Fraternity and its chapters. It is adopted at the Convention of 1894. Before this the badge and the colours were the only uniform symbolism Psi Upsilon had.

title: A second brother in the White House
text: William Howard Taft, Beta 1878, becomes President of the United States. He is later Chief Justice of the Supreme Court — the only man to hold both offices — and it was largely at his urging that Psi Upsilon chartered its first chapter outside the United States.

title: The first Heisman Trophy
text: Jay Berwanger, Omega 1936, wins the first Heisman Trophy and becomes the first player selected in the first NFL draft.

title: The Annals of Psi Upsilon
text: The Fraternity's centennial history is published in twelve parts. Much of what is known about the founders comes from it.

title: The last printed Diamond
text: The final printed issue of The Diamond appears, closing a run that began in 1878.
